title: Who Is Russia’s New Ambassador to North Korea?
author: Piergiorgio Pescali
text:
Shortly after his arrival in Pyongyang, Russian Ambassador to North Korea Andrei Podelyshev pays respects at the memorial honoring North Korean troops killed fighting alongside Russian forces, Sep. 26, 2026.
Credit: X/ Russian Embassy in the DPRK
Russia has finally filled the ambassadorial post in Pyongyang, which had sat vacant for nearly eight months. Under a decree signed by President Vladimir Putin on July 28, career diplomat Andrei Podelyshev – at the time, Russia’s ambassador to Nigeria, a post he had held since December 2024 – was named the new ambassador extraordinary and plenipotentiary to the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea. A companion decree released him from his Nigerian posting the same day.Podelyshev arrived in Pyongyang nearly two months later, on September 26, together with his wife, aboard a direct Nordwind flight from Moscow. According to the Russian Embassy and TASS, he headed straight from the airport to the Soviet-era Liberation Monument to pay tribute to fallen Red Army soldiers, before visiting Pyongyang’s newly built memorial complex for North Korean troops killed fighting alongside Russian forces in Kursk.[...]
